# Decoding the Evaluation Matrix under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 ![](https://img.youtube.com/vi/I1Nc33LC_JE/hqdefault.jpg) 25 minutes ago (Jul 8, 2024) — 1:02:32 [https://youtube.com/watch?v=I1Nc33LC_JE](https://youtube.com/watch?v=I1Nc33LC_JE)

## Summary Today's webinar discusses the evaluation matrix, a concept in Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) in India. The evaluation matrix is used for evaluating resolution plans received during a CIRP by the Committee of Creditors (CoC). The parameters for evaluation are approved by the CoC and can be qualitative or quantitative. The purpose of the evaluation matrix is to ensure a transparent and efficient resolution process. The Institute of Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) and Insolvency Professional Agencies (IPAs) have released formats for the evaluation matrix. However, these formats cannot be considered as fit for all cases. The RP issues the information memorandum, evaluation matrix, and request for proposal (RFRP) to every resolution applicant in the final list. The CoC evaluates the resolution plans as per the evaluation matrix, and records its deliberations on the feasibility and viability of each resolution plan. The importance of the evaluation matrix has been lowered by judicial pronouncements, which state that the commercial wisdom of the CoC is Paramount. The evaluation matrix is not one fit for all, and the format discussed in the webinar is not available in the public domain. The primary objective of the CoC is giving maximum weightage to recovery rather than resolving the CD, and the RP can influence and educate the CoC in this aspect.
